title: BDL Basic Circular No. 170: Preventive measures to protect the financial and economic sector in Lebanon from dealing with unlicensed entities subjected to sanctions issued by foreign authorities
text:
Basic Circular No. 170
Addressed to Banks, Finance Companies, and all other Institutions regulated by
the Banque du Liban,
And also to Financial Intermediation Institutions and Collective Investment Schemes
Attached is a copy of Basic Decision No. 13735 of 14 July 2025, on Preventive Measures to
Protect the Financial and Economic Sector in Lebanon from Dealing with Unlicensed Entities
Subjected to Sanctions Issued by Foreign Authorities.
Beirut, 14 July 2025
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid

Basic Decision No. 13735
Preventive Measures to Protect the Financial and Economic Sector in Lebanon from
Dealing with Unlicensed Entities Subjected to Sanctions Issued by Foreign Authorities
The Governor of the Banque du Liban,
Pursuant to the Code of Money and Credit, particularly Articles 70, 174, 182, and 184
thereof;
Pursuant to the provisions of Law No. 44 of 24 November 2015 on Fighting Money
Laundering and Terrorist Financing, particularly Article 4 thereof;
Pursuant to the provisions of Law No. 161 of 17 August 2011 on Capital Markets;
Pursuant to the Business Conduct Regulations issued by the Capital Markets Authority
(CMA) in Lebanon on 10 November 2016;
Considering that the Code of Money and Credit and the relevant Circulars issued by the
Banque du Liban forbid to engage in any banking or financial activity without a prior
license from the Banque du Liban;
Pursuant to the provisions of Basic Decision No. 10965 of 5 April 2012 on the relationship
of banks and finance companies with correspondents (attached to Basic Circular No. 126
to Banks);
Pursuant to the provisions of Basic Decision No. 12253 of 3 May 2016 on dealing with the
US Act of 18 December 2015 and with its implementing regulations (attached to Basic
Circular No. 137 to Banks);
Considering that the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has placed Lebanon on the
grey list of “jurisdictions under increased monitoring” due to the deficiency and/or
weakness of implemented measures;
Considering that the FATF action plan for Lebanon consists in addressing the situation
of the unlicensed financial sector, in particular money exchange institutions, money
remittance companies, and associations engaging in financial and banking transactions
without a license from the Banque du Liban;
Since engaging in transactions with unlicensed entities subjected to international
sanctions, especially if these are part of a series of suspicious transactions that might
involve the licensed financial sector, without its knowledge, in crimes of money
laundering and/or terrorism financing;
To prevent further increased monitoring against the financial and economic sectors in
Lebanon and abroad;
1

To avoid any legal violation that correspondent banks may be exposed to and may
adversely affect the relationship with them;
To preserve the utmost national interest; and
Pursuant to the powers vested in the Governor to ensure the smooth running of the
Banque du Liban, based on the principle of the continous functioning of the public utility;
Decides the following:
Article 1:
Banks, finance companies, and all other institutions licensed by the Banque du Liban, as well
as financial intermediation institutions and collective investment schemes, are prohibited from
engaging in any financial, commercial, or similar activity, whether directly or indirectly, totally
or partially, with unlicensed money exchange institutions, money remittance companies,
associations, and organizations, such as “Al-Qard Al-Hassan”, “Tashilat SARL”, “Yousser
Company for Finance and Investment”, “Bayt al-Mal Lil Muslimeen”, and other institutions,
organizations, companies, entities, and associations designated on international sanctions lists,
mainly in terms of:
- Providing or facilitating financial or cash services, transfers, or intermediation services.
- Concluding or executing financing, rental, or lending arrangements.
- Facilitating the direct or indirect access of the above-mentioned associations,
organizations, or companies, and any other similar entity, or their branches, to the
Lebanese banking system, in any currency.
Article 2:
Non-compliance with the provisions of this Decision shall expose its infringers to legal actions
and measures that may reach to the extent of:
- License suspension or withdrawal
- Freezing of accounts and assets
- Referral to the Special Investigation Commission (SIC)
Article 3:
The Banque du Liban asserts that it shall take all proper administrative and legal measures to
impose the implementation of the provisions of this Decision.
Article 4:
This Decision shall enter into force upon its issuance.
2

Article 5:
This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette.
Beirut, 14 July 2025
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid
3
